A1.label: PlayArea.on_control_focus_entered — mouse hover grabs focus, so focus is the ONE hover signal for mouse, keyboard and pad

A3.label: PlayArea._show_focus_info — a 260 px panel pinned beside the card, re-pinned every frame

A4.label: PlayArea._on_gui_input — left click on the focused card

A5.label: PlayArea._info_mode true, so info_requested carries card_info instead of data_selected — the click performs NO game action

A8.label: InfoCard.show_entry — the ONE notecard, anchored to the bottom of the WINDOW

A9.label: Main._on_info_toggled — the camera animates to WallPicture.info_zoom_state

A10.label: Map._on_node_hovered — MapHoverPanel.get_info, published and nothing else

B1.label: NEW — a highlight arrives: mouse hover, or keyboard and pad selection. Same rule for both

B2.label: NEW — the container swaps its contents to the description, instantly, no animation — chart C

B3.label: NEW — an ARMED card alone does not open it. Arming is not highlighting

B4.label: NEW — pointer leaves everything with nothing locked: the description STAYS, showing the last entry, so it never blinks in and out

B5.label: NEW — a click on a card LOCKS the description to it, and the same click still performs its game action — chart E

B6.label: NEW — locked, and the pointer moves to another card

B7.label: NEW — the description follows the hover, and returns to the locked card once the pointer leaves everything

B8.label: NEW — locking a second card replaces the first. Only one lock exists

B10.label: NEW — dismissing REVERTS the container to the HUD. Nothing is hidden, because the container is always on screen

B11.label: NEW — the held card's cursor leaves the bounds of the cell it came from

B12.label: NEW — the card is placed: the interaction is finished, so the description closes

B13.label: NEW — a board rebuild keeps the same CardData's description, whichever control now represents it

B14.label: NEW — the win or lose screen leaves the description open, so a card can still be read beside the result

B15.label: NEW — leaving the screen closes it, and each screen REMEMBERS its own last description

B16.label: NEW — coming back re-shows that description immediately, exactly as it was left

C1.label: NEW — one real PanelContainer with a flat background and no border. Art later; the container is what makes art possible

C3.label: NEW — inside the HUD, top to bottom: the numbers first, then the piles as one ROW across the width, then the actions

C4.label: NEW — members: Deck, Discard, Rules, Goal, Total, Combo, Undo, End. %MultScore and %Preview are DELETED in the same pass — chart L

C5.label: NEW — a highlight arrives, so the contents swap to the description — chart B

C6.label: NEW — while the description shows, the HUD's controls are off screen. Accepted

C7.label: NEW — a LOCKED description is forced back to the HUD by cancel

C8.label: NEW — the panel eats clicks in its whole rect, which today's scattered controls do not

C9.label: NEW — no hud_scale. The container lays out to its own rect, so the scale mechanism and both authored-offset caches go

C10.label: NEW — the MAP gets the same container, holding Fame, Lap, Luck and its Deck button, which is what makes the geometry identical on both screens — chart K

C11.label: The debug bar and the prop-step controls stay OUTSIDE it, top-right, unchanged

C12.label: GameView win or lose overlay still covers ONLY the play area, so the container stays live

C13.label: NEW — the exit X in the container's top-right means GO BACK TO THE HUD, at the touch-target minimum

D1.label: NEW — ONE knob: the container's width as a fraction of the WINDOW. hud_width_fraction is retired

D2.label: NEW — would the play area LEFT OVER be taller than it is wide

D3.label: NEW — the container is on the LEFT, full window height

D4.label: NEW — the container moves to the TOP, where the HUD also is, so the main playing window stays as square as possible

D5.label: NEW — at the top the same fraction is read as a HEIGHT

D6.label: NEW — is the window wide enough that the fraction exceeds the maximum

D7.label: NEW — clamped, and the clamp is measured INWARD: the container sits flush against the inner edge of its band, so it stays near the middle and the empty space is on its far side

D8.label: NEW — PlayArea.board_inset_left becomes the container's width, converted from window pixels to picture pixels through the focused picture's live scale

D9.label: NEW — a matching TOP inset exists for the case where the container moved up

D10.label: NEW — the board centres in what is left, never on the screen

D11.label: The MAP uses the window fraction directly: it has no picture and needs no conversion

D12.label: NEW — the overlay's Back, Forward and Wall buttons draw ON TOP of the container and stay pressable

D13.label: InfoCard._reposition_to_window — the same re-anchor on resize, keeping its content

D14.label: NEW — the container does NOT pan with the board. GameView._process's furniture slide and PlayArea.pan_window_left_x are both deleted — chart L

E1.label: NEW — what is under the click

E2.label: NEW — an ENTRANCE card: re-arms it AND locks its description, in one click

E3.label: NEW — a CELL, and is a card armed

E4.label: NEW — armed: the card is placed immediately, one click, no confirm — and on touch too, because it is undoable and hesitation is worse

E6.label: NEW — occupied: the card STACKS, and the legal-cell highlight already showed that it would

E7.label: NEW — nothing armed: the click opens that cell's description if it holds a card

E8.label: NEW — a BOARD card: it is grabbed, but only after the armed card has been cancelled first, because otherwise the click would try to place onto it

E9.label: NEW — if the board card is not stackable, picking it up is the only remaining action, so the grab is allowed straight away

E10.label: NEW — while a board card is held, the Entrance DISARMS until it is put down

E11.label: NEW — the grab is the primary feedback: the card lifts and follows the cursor, and the description updates quietly behind it

E13.label: NEW — the HELD CARD is released first

E14.label: NEW — a second press then dismisses the description — chart B

E15.label: NEW — Escape does MORE than cancel: it cancels everything the second button would AND shows the menu or wall immediately

E16.label: NEW — on a touchscreen the FIRST tap behaves as a hover, so nothing commits on it

F1.label: Godot delivers an ORDINARY click first: Windows sends WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK in place of the second press, so by the time a tap is recognised the card is already grabbed

F2.label: NEW — the tap UNDOES that first click's grab

F3.label: NEW — a tap arriving after a PLACEMENT is refused outright. A placement can never be rewound by a double-click

F4.label: NEW — on touch the project detects the double-tap itself, from two screen presses within a time window and a distance window, because Godot never sets double_tap on a Windows touchscreen

F5.label: NEW — on keyboard and pad, BOTH: a double-press of the normal button, and a separate bindable action of its own

F6.label: NEW — a double-click on an ENTRANCE card taps it, and the arm still stands

F7.label: NEW — an empty cell's zone card taps too, because zone cards carry modifiers

F8.label: NEW — a tapped signal is emitted. Nothing in the game listens in v1 except one dummy effect built for testing

F9.label: NEW — the second mouse button is cancel-only. It no longer taps, which is what DESIGN_DOC section 12 originally planned — chart E

G1.label: NEW — the LEFTMOST card present in the Entrance arms automatically, matching the refill's own left-to-right order

G2.label: NEW — armed means MARKED IN ITS SLOT. It lifts only once the pointer is over the board

G3.label: NEW — GLOW means selected. LIFT means currently picked up, which warns that the next click on a highlighted space will put the lifted card down

G4.label: NEW — the selection glow sits wherever the selector is, showing the current selection as normal

G5.label: NEW — arming does NOT open the armed card's description. Only a real highlight does — chart B

G6.label: NEW — every legal cell is highlighted, and because a card is armed for the whole show, that highlight is on for the whole show

G7.label: Game.place_card_in_grid — the placement commits the Entrance to its grid, exactly as today. Arming commits nothing

G8.label: NEW — after a placement, the new leftmost present card arms

G9.label: NEW — after a refill, the new leftmost card arms — chart I

G10.label: NEW — cancel DISARMS, and clicks on cells then do nothing until something is armed again

G11.label: NEW — the arm is view-only. Undo restores the board and the arm is re-derived as leftmost present

G12.label: NEW — keyboard and pad: the arm replaces the old select-an-Entrance-card step, and the arrows go straight to aiming a cell cursor

G13.label: NEW — every slot's stock empty: nothing arms, and clicks on cells do nothing — chart H

H1.label: NEW — each Entrance slot owns its OWN ordered stock. The single draw deck is replaced by them

H2.label: Game.shuffle_deck — the one shuffle the game already does, unchanged

H3.label: NEW — the shuffled deck is DEALT round-robin, left to right, so earlier slots take the extras when the count does not divide

H4.label: NEW — this happens at show start, and again whenever the SET of slots changes

H5.label: NEW — no new RNG anywhere, so the resume-replay ruling holds exactly as it does today

H7.label: NEW — a slot was REMOVED: its cards go from ITS BOTTOM, round-robin, to the BOTTOMS of the remaining slots, left to right

H8.label: NEW — a slot was ADDED: the bottom card of each existing slot in turn, round-robin, until the new slot has its even share

H9.label: NEW — TOPS NEVER MOVE. What is about to be drawn is stable, so a peek effect stays honest

H10.label: NEW — the rebalance is silent. It is bookkeeping under face-down cards and nothing visible moves

H11.label: NEW — a slot whose stock exhausts stays empty. Exhaustion never triggers a rebalance

H12.label: NEW — no caller adds or removes a slot yet. This is machinery built for a future card effect, deliberately with no caller today

H13.label: NEW — stocks are part of the board: on_append and every board walk reach their cards exactly as they reach the draw deck today

H14.label: NEW — an in-flight save written before this change is DISCARDED, not migrated

H15.label: Game.return_to_map — the discard is still swept back only when the show ends

I1.label: Game.refill_entrance_if_due — the trigger is unchanged: the Entrance is empty, OR no held card has a legal placement

I2.label: TypeInput.on_refill — each header still fills its own slot if that slot is empty, left to right by dispatch order

I3.label: NEW — the card comes off the top of THAT SLOT'S OWN STOCK — chart H

I4.label: NEW — every slot holding a face-down card FLIPS IT UP IN PLACE, staggered left to right to match the draw order

I5.label: NEW — the stagger is a knob, as a fraction of get_delay per slot, never a wall-clock literal

I6.label: NEW — slots still holding a face-up card do NOTHING. Only empty slots flip

I7.label: NEW — there is no fly-in from the Deck control any more

I8.label: NEW — a capped stack of face-down cards is drawn, so depth reads at a glance. The cap is a knob defaulting to 5

I9.label: NEW — a slot with nothing left shows an empty slot frame, which is what the Entrance already shows

I10.label: NEW — hovering a face-down stock describes the SLOT, not a card: how many remain in this stock — chart B

I11.label: NEW — a bonus reveal simply DEEPENS that slot's face-up stack, since the Entrance already holds a stack per slot

I12.label: NEW — the Deck button shows the union of every stock as ONE list, sorted by suit and rank so no ordering leaks

J1.label: Game.place_card_in_grid — a placement resolves: every line scored, every prop tick finished

J2.label: GameData.has_met_goal — the check fires once the WHOLE placement has settled, never mid-cascade

J3.label: NEW — the Goal label changes state the moment the total passes it, so the ending is announced rather than sprung

J4.label: NEW — a short pause, so the final score lands visibly

J5.label: Game.end_show — the same flag, the same save, the same resolve the End button drives today

J6.label: NEW — there is no declining. Reaching the goal ends the show, full stop

J7.label: Game.exit_show — Continue still banks the fame, so the outcome stays undoable

J8.label: NEW — the End button SURVIVES, for a show that can no longer be won

J9.label: NEW — End is REVEALED when either the deck is empty, or no more action is possible on the board

J10.label: A full board still does NOT end a show: cards may remain in the Entrance and effects may free cells

J11.label: Game.undo — rewinds an automatic end exactly as it rewinds a manual one, back to the live board

J12.label: Resume lands on the outcome screen, because show_ended is saved before the resolve

K2.label: NEW — a small popup appears with the node's NAME ONLY, directly above the node, centred, and it stays put

K3.label: NEW — the same hover ALSO fills the sidebar with everything else — chart B

K4.label: Map._on_node_entered — a click still ENTERS the node, exactly as today. Travelling never costs a second click

K5.label: NEW — on a touchscreen the first tap is the same as a hover, so it describes rather than travels

K6.label: NEW — after the pointer leaves, the sidebar keeps the last node's description, the same persistence the board has

K7.label: MapHoverPanel.get_info — the entry is now ALWAYS used, so the old build-and-throw-away waste is gone

K8.label: NEW — a booster's preview cards are a flowing grid that wraps to the sidebar's width and scrolls with the rest

K9.label: NEW — hovering one of those preview cards switches the sidebar to that CARD, with a way back to the pack

K10.label: NEW — keyboard and pad: a node cursor, and whatever is selected is described. Same rule as the board

K11.label: NEW — no small popup on the board. It is a map affordance, for nodes that are just dots

K12.label: NEW — the sidebar is on the same side as the game's, always — chart D

L1.label: wall_info_mode, the wall_info InputMap action, and the overlay's magnifying-glass Info toggle

L2.label: WallPicture.info_zoom_state and WallTransition's info branch — the zoom-out goes with them

L5.label: Tools/wall_editor.tscn's Info panel becomes a SIDEBAR preview panel: width, side, opacity and the exit X, live against a real hosted screen

L6.label: Tests/Wall/test_wall_info and Tests/Visual/wall_info_snapshot are REPLACED by sidebar equivalents, so coverage does not drop

L8.label: GameView._process's furniture pan, its two authored-offset caches, hud_scale, and PlayArea.pan_window_left_x

L9.label: %MultScore with its Col, x and Row children, and %Preview

L10.label: hud_width_fraction, replaced by the container's own window fraction — chart D

L11.label: The deck, discard and rules viewers' own description panels, which publish to the sidebar instead

L12.label: GameData.draw_deck as the single deck, replaced by per-slot stocks — chart H

L13.label: UI/deck_builder.gd is REPAIRED, not deleted: new classes, dead code removed, the tool itself kept

edges.label: not in Info mode AND wall_screen_popups
in Info mode: this panel always yields
